headline: Green chilli prices drop by over 50% as imports resume
summary: Prices in Dhaka markets have fallen to 180-200 BDT per kg after the government allowed imports from India to stabilize the market.
details: Green chilli prices in Bangladesh have begun to decrease following the resumption of imports from India. On Monday, 100 metric tons of chillies were imported through the Bhomra land port.

In Dhaka's retail markets, prices have dropped to between 180 and 200 BDT per kg. This follows a period where prices surged to as high as 400 BDT per kg due to low domestic production caused by adverse weather.
Wholesalers report that the supply of Indian green chillies through various land ports has increased local availability, directly impacting retail prices.

Traders are now securing import permits (IP) and opening letters of credit (LC) to maintain the supply. Local importers are also coordinating with Indian exporters to ensure a steady flow of produce into the country.
caption:
From 400 BDT to 180 BDT—green chilli prices have plummeted after imports from India resumed.

Green chilli prices in Bangladesh have begun to decrease following the resumption of imports from India. On Monday, 100 metric tons of chillies were imported through the Bhomra land port.

In Dhaka's retail markets, prices have dropped to between 180 and 200 BDT per kg. This follows a period where prices surged to as high as 400 BDT per kg due to low domestic production caused by adverse weather.

Wholesalers report that the supply of Indian green chillies through various land ports has increased local availability, directly impacting retail prices.

Traders are now securing import permits (IP) and opening letters of credit (LC) to maintain the supply. Local importers are also coordinating with Indian exporters to ensure a steady flow of produce into the country.

headline: Around 50 injured as student wings clash at Jagannath University
summary: Activists from JCD, Shibir, and Jatiya Chhatra Shakti clashed on campus today, leading to injuries among student leaders and journalists.
details: Around 50 people, including student leaders and journalists, were reportedly injured during a clash between Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal (JCD), Bangladesh Islami Chhatra Shibir, and Jatiya Chhatra Shakti at Jagannath University (JnU).

The violence broke out around 11:30 am during a documentary screening attended by UGC Chairman Prof SMA Faiz. The clash began when JCD activists stopped JnUCSU and Inquilab Mancha members from entering the venue with placards.
The protesters were demanding that the construction of the university's second campus be handed over to the army and calling for improved medical facilities at the university's medical centre.
JnUCSU General Secretary Abdul Alim Arif alleged that JCD activists attacked them with sticks and vandalised the university's medical centre, claiming some teachers may have backed the attackers.
JCD unit Member Secretary Shamsul Arefin rejected these claims, stating that general students resisted the attempt to create a 'mob situation' on campus.
Jatiya Chhatra Shakti President Shahin Mia reported that 10 to 12 people from their group were injured, including himself and General Secretary Ferdous Sheikh.
University Proctor Prof Nasir Uddin stated that an investigation is underway to determine if 'anti-July forces' or banned Chhatra League activists were involved in the disorder.
Sutrapur Police Station confirmed that the situation on and around the campus had returned to calm by early afternoon.
caption:
Around 50 people, including journalists and student leaders, injured in a violent clash at Jagannath University.

Around 50 people, including student leaders and journalists, were reportedly injured during a clash between Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal (JCD), Bangladesh Islami Chhatra Shibir, and Jatiya Chhatra Shakti at Jagannath University (JnU).

The violence broke out around 11:30 am during a documentary screening attended by UGC Chairman Prof SMA Faiz. The clash began when JCD activists stopped JnUCSU and Inquilab Mancha members from entering the venue with placards.

The protesters were demanding that the construction of the university's second campus be handed over to the army and calling for improved medical facilities at the university's medical centre.

JnUCSU General Secretary Abdul Alim Arif alleged that JCD activists attacked them with sticks and vandalised the university's medical centre, claiming some teachers may have backed the attackers.

JCD unit Member Secretary Shamsul Arefin rejected these claims, stating that general students resisted the attempt to create a 'mob situation' on campus.

Jatiya Chhatra Shakti President Shahin Mia reported that 10 to 12 people from their group were injured, including himself and General Secretary Ferdous Sheikh.

University Proctor Prof Nasir Uddin stated that an investigation is underway to determine if 'anti-July forces' or banned Chhatra League activists were involved in the disorder.

Sutrapur Police Station confirmed that the situation on and around the campus had returned to calm by early afternoon.
